name: astra
description: ASTRA methodology plugin. Sprint 0 project initialization, automatic coding convention enforcement (Java/TypeScript/React Native/Python/CSS/SCSS), Korean public data standard, international code standards (ISO 3166-1/2, ITU-T E.164), naming validation, quality gates, Slack integration, service manual auto-generation, UX/UI/Dev/QA Screen-ID based Handoff package auto-generation (HANDOFF_PROCESS_GUIDE v1.1), role-based persona agents (planner / designer / developer / tester validation and delegation), and the /autorun self-improving pipeline (planning → test auto-execution + up to N iteration self-improvement loop, with early termination on test pass). v5.12.0: /uat-parallel skill added — Playwright-powered parallel sibling of /user-test. Reuses 100% of docs/tests/uat-cases/*.md format and the /user-test HTML report template (same docs/tests/uat-reports/{SESSION_ID}/ output layout). Each worker holds an isolated BrowserContext (separate cookies / localStorage / sessionStorage); per-step + per-case hard timeouts kill stuck cases without blocking other workers. Bootstraps @playwright/test + chromium on first run via single AskUserQuestion. Args: --workers N (default min(4, cpu/2)) / --from / --priority / --feature / --timeout / --headed / --browser. Auto-batch only — no interactive mode. Failed cases yield Playwright trace .zip archives (replayable via `npx playwright show-trace`). Severity assignment mirrors user-test assertion-guide.md §3. Solves /user-test's two main limits: sequential single-page execution doesn't scale, and a stuck case blocks the run. v5.11.2: /pr-merge Step 8.4.5.1 (post-merge promotion-path prompt) now always fires AskUserQuestion, even under --auto — the merge target branch where the integration branch finally lands (dev / staging / skip) is a deployment-surface decision with no safe unattended default. /autorun and /sprint-init --auto now treat this as a routine HITL pause; the pipeline still completes end-to-end in a single invocation, but the user picks the target. Direct integration → main remains gated behind the explicit /pr-merge --main promotion. v5.11.1: integration-branch model extended to --staging/--main promotion modes. v5.11.0: integration-branch model for /pr-merge. Sprint PRs (head=feat/sprint-*) target a feature- or fix-level integration branch (feat/<name> or fix/<name>) chosen interactively in Step 4.5 — pick from existing branches (top 3 by activity) or create new with user-chosen base (default origin/dev). Classification (feat/fix) and slug auto-inferred from commit prefixes, sprint slug, and blueprint keywords. New Step 8.4.5 asks promotion path after sprint→integration merge: 'dev (standard, default)' / 'staging (fast hotfix)' / 'skip'; chosen promotion creates a second PR with no fresh review. Integration branches are persistent (Step 9 protects them from auto-delete). /sprint-init Step 1.5 also became interactive — sprint source branch is user-chosen (default dev; staging/main/master/custom). Step 3.5 PR detection query updated with backward-compat fallback to base=dev. Under --auto: integration reuse-or-create-from-dev, promotion=dev, sprint source=dev — /autorun and /sprint-init --auto still complete end-to-end. Trade-off: one sprint = up to 2 PRs; benefit: feature-level promotion granularity for hotfix paths. v5.10.0: /blueprint reordered to worktree-first — Step 1.5 branch/location guards (non-standard branch aborts with error; sprint worktree reused), Step 1.6 delegates to /sprint-init --scaffold-only to create the worktree first, Step 1.7 cd's into it, Steps 2-6 author + review + commit the blueprint *inside* the sprint branch (not dev). /sprint-init --scaffold-only flag (new) suppresses prompt-map Feature 1.1 and renumbers remaining steps as 1.1=DB Design, 1.2=Test Cases, 1.3=Implementation; incompatible with --auto. Backward-compat: --from-blueprint aliased to --scaffold-only. /autorun Stage 4 becomes a no-op since /blueprint already creates the worktree. CLAUDE.md + commands/blueprint.md updated. v5.9.0: /user-test skill added — AI-assisted UAT for end-user flows. Drives Chrome MCP with hard-assertion verification (URL / Network / DOM / Console) and auto-assigns severity per a fixed rule table. Two modes: interactive (URL + Vietnamese natural-language flow, generates draft test case) and --auto (batch-runs pre-authored cases under docs/tests/uat-cases/, filterable by --priority / --feature / --from). Output: timestamped docs/tests/uat-reports/{YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm}/ folder with index.html, issues.md (only on failure), session.json. On FAIL the case is skipped and the run continues. Progressive disclosure into references/assertion-guide.md and assets/report-template.html. Distinct from /test-run (developer technical tests) and /test-scenario (scenario authoring). Runtime language follows /select-language; default Vietnamese. v5.9.0: /pr-merge two-phase policy — `gh pr merge` only runs from the main worktree. Sprint Phase (inside the sprint worktree) handles PR creation + code review + fix loop and stops; the user `cd`s to the main worktree and re-invokes `/pr-merge` to finalize the merge + worktree removal (auto-detects pending sprint PRs). `--auto` chains both phases automatically. Multi-PR detection preserves AskUserQuestion even under --auto. Promotion modes unchanged. v5.7.0: /tool-author skill added for runtime LLM tool surface authoring + validation (Anthropic Tool Use, MCP, LangChain @tool, Pydantic, Zod). Enforces 6 required attributes and blocks 7 failure modes (wrong-tool selection, skipped tool, malformed args, retry loops, intent bypass, wrong side-effect, un-auditable traces). Auto-trigger via paths (tools/**, mcp/**, **/tools.py, src/**/*.tool.ts). Distinct from /skill-author (which targets ASTRA SKILL.md files). v5.6.0: /pr-merge cascade merge restricted to `staging → dev` only — `main → staging` is no longer auto-cascaded; `main` is touched only via the explicit `--main` promotion. Promotion modes (`--staging`, `--main`) skip the cascade entirely. Training docs (branch-strategy 1pager / ko / vi) and CLAUDE.md updated to reflect the new single-hop cascade flow. v5.5.0: Full English localization of plugin internals (skills, commands, agents, hooks, scripts, docs, CLAUDE.md). Skill description language policy now mandates English for all skills (auto-trigger accuracy + consistency). Runtime end-user output language remains controlled by /select-language (Korean / Vietnamese / English). Korean public-data dictionary terms, prefixes/suffixes (TB_, _YMD, etc.), and dictionary field names (공통표준용어명, etc.) are preserved as data definitions. v5.4.0: DESIGN.md design system SSoT introduced (Google Stitch + ASTRA 3-tier hybrid). Four new skills/commands — /design-init (generates DESIGN.md + auto-regenerates design-tokens.css), /design-extract (extracts OKLCH tokens from image/PDF/URL references), /design-redesign (audits UI against DESIGN.md + applies P0 fixes automatically), /design-audit (lightweight token-violation report). design-token-validator now recognizes DESIGN.md as SSoT and treats design-tokens.css as a generated artifact. /service-planner Step E loads DESIGN.md first; /handoff-publish 6-component-specs.md references DESIGN.md §4. PostToolUse hook (notify-design-md.sh) added to advise DESIGN.md consultation on UI code edits — throttled, non-blocking. v5.3.0: Plugin-required MCPs reorganized — `fect-slack` removed from plugin-required MCPs (still usable via user-scope MCP registration by /slack-import, /extract-backlog, /sprint-progress); `fect-image` (Gemini, requires GOOGLE_API_KEY) and `fect-gpt-image` (OpenAI gpt-image-2, requires OPENAI_API_KEY) added for AI image generation; `chrome-devtools` (chrome-devtools-mcp@latest) MCP added as a first-class required MCP for /manual-generator screenshots, /catalog-generator visual capture, and /test-run browser-based integration testing. SessionStart hook updated to report GOOGLE_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY activation status. v5.2.0: /sprint-init --auto stage-to-stage flow replaced from 'exit + user --resume' pattern with 'Silent Save Protocol (save auto-state.yaml + commit, then continue automatically to next stage)'. The LLM avoids re-referencing large prior artifacts (reference-avoidance) so Claude Code's built-in auto-compression works effectively. --resume is now reserved strictly for true recovery (context loss, crash, forced interrupt). v5.1.0: /blueprint dedicated skill added — 10 standard-section blueprint focused on data flow, schema, API contract, sequence diagrams, and pseudocode logic (no executable code). Section 10 'HITL Triggers' gates HITL invocation during /feature-dev's implementation phase. /sprint-init prompt-map Step 1.1 and /autorun Stage 3 delegate to the new skill. v4.0.0: /ux-publish removed; HTML mockup generation integrated into /service-planner Step 6.

plugins.description: ASTRA methodology plugin with coding convention enforcement, data standard, international code standards, naming validation, quality gates, Slack integration, service manual auto-generator, UX/UI/Dev/QA Screen-ID based handoff package generator, role-based persona agents, and /autorun self-improving full pipeline. v5.12.0 NEW: /uat-parallel skill — Playwright-powered parallel sibling of /user-test. Reuses 100% of docs/tests/uat-cases/*.md format and the /user-test HTML report template (same docs/tests/uat-reports/{SESSION_ID}/ layout with index.html, issues.md, session.json, screenshots/). Each worker holds an isolated BrowserContext (separate cookies / localStorage / sessionStorage) so multi-user flows and race conditions do not collide; per-step hard timeout (UAT_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30s) + per-case timeout (UAT_CASE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 300s) kill stuck cases without blocking other workers. Bootstraps @playwright/test + chromium on first run via a single AskUserQuestion HITL (~150 MB). Args: --workers N (default min(4, cpu/2)) / --from / --priority / --feature / --timeout / --headed / --browser chromium|firefox|webkit. No interactive mode — auto-batch only. Runtime artifacts copied idempotently into .astra/uat/ (uat-runner.spec.ts + playwright.config.ts) on every invocation. Severity assignment in the runner mirrors user-test/references/assertion-guide.md §3 (CRITICAL 5xx / Uncaught; HIGH 4xx primary + 401/403 + no URL change; MEDIUM missing CTA + text mismatch; LOW default). Failed cases yield Playwright trace .zip archives at traces/{UAT-ID}.zip — replayable via `npx playwright show-trace ...` for DOM/network/console timeline debugging that Chrome MCP cannot produce. Solves the two main /user-test limits: sequential single-page execution doesn't scale beyond a few cases, and a stuck case blocks the rest of the run. References progressive-disclosure into parallel-guide.md (worker tuning, isolation guarantees, debugging flaky cases, CI integration sketch). v5.11.2 NEW: /pr-merge Step 8.4.5.1 (post-merge promotion-path prompt — dev / staging / skip) now always fires AskUserQuestion, even under --auto. Previously --auto silently picked dev; the merge target branch where the integration branch finally lands is a deployment-surface decision with no safe unattended default. /autorun and /sprint-init --auto now treat this as a routine HITL pause — pipeline still completes end-to-end in a single invocation but the user picks the target. Direct integration → main is intentionally NOT offered here (the explicit /pr-merge --main promotion, with version bump + release checks, remains the only production path). All other --auto behaviors (commit confirmation, final-merge approval, Step 4.5 integration auto-pick, Step 4.5.4 base auto-pick, Step 10.0 promotion-source defaults) are unchanged. v5.11.1 NEW: integration-branch model extended to --staging and --main promotion modes. New Step 10.0 asks the promotion source — legacy bulk (dev for --staging, staging for --main) OR a specific integration branch (feat/<name>/fix/<name>) from top-3 most-recent — so urgent hotfixes can land ONLY that feature on staging or directly on main without dragging other staging changes. Integration-source promotions skip Step 8 code review (already passed on source sprint PRs); bulk sources keep the review loop. Step 10.1 PR body varies by source type for traceability. Under --auto: --staging defaults to dev, --main defaults to staging (legacy paths preserved). v5.11.0 NEW: integration-branch model for /pr-merge — sprint PRs no longer target dev directly. The new Step 4.5 picks a feature- or fix-level integration branch (feat/<name> or fix/<name>) interactively: pick from top 3 existing branches by recent activity, or create new with user-chosen base (default origin/dev; options include origin/staging, origin/main, origin/master, custom). Classification (feat vs fix) and slug auto-inferred from Conventional Commit prefixes on the sprint branch, sprint-slug keywords, and blueprint §1+§10 keyword scan. After sprint PR merges into the integration branch, the new Step 8.4.5 asks the promotion path: 'dev (standard, default)' / 'staging (fast hotfix)' / 'skip' — a promotion PR is created and merged without fresh code review (sprint PR already passed). Integration branches are PERSISTENT — Step 9 explicit guard prevents auto-deletion; only feat/sprint-* and fix/sprint-* are eligible for git branch -d. Step 3.5 query updated to filter PRs by head~feat/sprint-* AND base~^(feat|fix)/ with backward-compat fallback to base=dev. /sprint-init Step 1.5 also became interactive — the sprint source branch is user-chosen (default dev; options staging/main/master/custom); passed through to astra_create_sprint_worktree. Under --auto: integration-branch selection reuses existing-name-matching else creates new from dev; promotion = dev; sprint source = dev — /autorun and /sprint-init --auto still complete end-to-end. Multiple-pending-PR detection preserves AskUserQuestion HITL even under --auto. Promotion modes (--staging, --main) and staging→dev cascade unaffected. Trade-off: one sprint = up to 2 PRs (sprint→integration, integration→target). Benefit: feature- or bugfix-level promotion granularity — urgent hotfixes land on staging directly without queuing through dev. v5.10.0 NEW: /blueprint worktree-first order — Step 1.5 enforces branch/location guards (non-standard branch aborts with error; already in sprint worktree → reused for secondary blueprints), Step 1.6 delegates to /sprint-init --scaffold-only to create the sprint worktree first, Step 1.7 cd's into it, and Steps 2-6 author + review + commit the blueprint *inside* the sprint worktree on the sprint branch (no dev commit). /sprint-init --scaffold-only is a new flag that (a) suppresses prompt-map Feature 1.1 (blueprint authoring) and renumbers remaining steps as 1.1=DB Design, 1.2=Test Cases, 1.3=Implementation (new Variant B), (b) is incompatible with --auto (no blueprint to drive auto pipeline), and (c) exits cleanly after Step 4 so the calling /blueprint owns the consolidated output. The legacy --from-blueprint flag is preserved as a backward-compat alias. /autorun Stage 3 unchanged in behavior since /blueprint now does the worktree creation; Stage 4 (/sprint-init re-entry) is an idempotent no-op in the standard path. commands/blueprint.md description + behavior summary table updated. CLAUDE.md Worktree Isolation section + Skill Catalog row + Recommended Workflow updated. Removes the v5.8/5.9 cross-branch dev-visibility commit logic — simpler invariants. v5.9.0 NEW: /user-test skill — AI-assisted UAT (User Acceptance Testing) for end-user flows. Drives Chrome MCP with hard-assertion verification (URL / Network / DOM / Console) and auto-assigns severity (CRITICAL / HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW) per a fixed rule table. Two modes: interactive (URL + Vietnamese natural-language flow description, generates draft test case and offers to save) and --auto (batch-runs pre-authored test cases under docs/tests/uat-cases/, filterable by --priority / --feature / --from). Output: timestamped session folder docs/tests/uat-reports/{YYYY-MM-DD-HHmm}/ with index.html (visual report + per-step thumbnails), issues.md (only when failures exist), session.json. On FAIL the case is skipped and the next case continues. Progressive disclosure into references/assertion-guide.md and assets/report-template.html. Distinct from /test-run (developer-authored technical integration tests) and /test-scenario (scenario authoring). Runtime output language follows /select-language; default Vietnamese. No GitHub Issue integration — local issues.md only. Also v5.9.0: /pr-merge two-phase policy. `gh pr merge` only runs from the main worktree. Sprint Phase (invoked inside a sprint worktree) handles commit → push → PR → review → fix loop and stops; the user `cd`s to the main worktree and re-invokes `/pr-merge`, which auto-detects the pending sprint PR (base=dev, head=feat/sprint-*) via Step 3.5 and finalizes the merge + worktree removal via Step M1. Step 8.5 (Sprint→Main handoff) and Step 8.3 (phase decision based on STARTED_FROM_SPRINT flag) are new. Under `--auto`, the skill itself `cd`s to the main worktree and continues into Main Phase so /autorun and /sprint-init --auto still complete end-to-end in one invocation. Multiple-pending-PR detection preserves AskUserQuestion even under --auto. Promotion modes (--staging, --main) are unaffected. v5.8.0 NEW: /blueprint Step 6.5 auto-creates the sprint worktree by delegating to /sprint-init at the end of authoring — the skill does NOT change the user's cwd (to avoid relying on unreliable Skill-to-Skill cwd propagation), and Step 7 output shows the user a concrete `cd .astra-worktrees/sprint-<N>-<slug>/` command to run next so they can enter the worktree explicitly. Two safety guards skip auto-creation: cwd already inside a sprint worktree (secondary blueprint flow), or current branch is not dev/main/master. /sprint-init recognizes a `--from-blueprint` flag to suppress duplicate output when delegated. /autorun Stage 4 became an idempotent re-entry — discovers the worktree via `git worktree list` and performs explicit cd itself (autorun is unattended), and falls back to explicit /sprint-init when the worktree was not auto-created. Legacy workflows (explicit /sprint-init → /blueprint inside worktree) remain fully supported. v5.7.0 NEW: /tool-author skill — authors and validates runtime LLM tool descriptions and input schemas (Anthropic Tool Use, MCP server.tool(), LangChain @tool, Pydantic, Zod). Enforces six required attributes and blocks seven failure modes (wrong-tool selection, skipped tool, malformed arguments, retry loops, user-intent bypass, wrong side-effect, un-auditable traces). Auto-trigger via tools/mcp path conventions. Scoped distinctly from /skill-author (which targets ASTRA SKILL.md files). v5.5.0 NEW: Full English localization of plugin internals (skills, commands, agents, hooks, scripts, docs, CLAUDE.md). Skill description language policy now mandates English for all skills (auto-trigger accuracy + consistency). Runtime end-user output language remains controlled by /select-language (Korean / Vietnamese / English). Korean public-data dictionary terms, prefixes/suffixes (TB_, _YMD, etc.), and dictionary field names (공통표준용어명, etc.) are preserved as data definitions. v5.4.0 NEW: DESIGN.md as design system SSoT — four new skills/commands (/design-init, /design-extract, /design-redesign, /design-audit). design-token-validator treats DESIGN.md as SSoT and src/styles/design-tokens.css as a generated artifact regenerable via `/design-init --regenerate-css`. /service-planner Step E loads DESIGN.md as primary token + persona source; /handoff-publish 6-component-specs.md references DESIGN.md §4. New PostToolUse hook notify-design-md.sh advises DESIGN.md consultation on UI source edits (throttled, non-blocking). /project-init bootstraps DESIGN.md during Sprint 0. v5.3.0 NEW: Required MCP servers reorganized — `fect-slack` removed from plugin-required MCPs (still consumed by /slack-import, /extract-backlog, /sprint-progress via user-scope MCP registration), `fect-image` (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, requires GOOGLE_API_KEY) and `fect-gpt-image` (OpenAI gpt-image-2, requires OPENAI_API_KEY) added for /catalog-generator image generation, and `chrome-devtools` (chrome-devtools-mcp@latest) added as a first-class required MCP for /manual-generator screenshots, /catalog-generator visual capture, and /test-run browser-based integration testing. v5.2.0 NEW: /sprint-init --auto now uses a Silent Save Protocol — between stages it writes auto-state.yaml + commits and continues directly to the next stage (no exit, no user --resume). A 'reference-avoidance' rule keeps the LLM from re-reading large prior artifacts so Claude Code's built-in auto-compression handles context. --resume is reserved for true crash/interrupt recovery. v5.1.0 NEW: /blueprint dedicated skill — 10 standard sections focused on data flow, schema DDL, API contract, sequence diagrams, pseudocode logic (no implementation code), plus a Section 10 'HITL Triggers' that /feature-dev consults during implementation to ask the user only on critical decisions (business decisions without a clear blueprint answer, security/permission choices, external dependency introduction, destructive changes). /sprint-init prompt-map Step 1.1 and /autorun Stage 3 now delegate to this skill. Single source of truth: the blueprint itself gates HITL — no external hook needed. v5.0.0 BREAKING: Sprint-level worktree model. /sprint-init creates `.astra-worktrees/sprint-<N>-<name>/` with sprint branch and port-isolated `.astra-worktree.env`; all dev + test happen inside the worktree. /test-run no longer touches dev — it sources the env, launches on the sprint port, and guarantees port release via 4-step cleanup. /pr-merge runs from the worktree, merges to dev, then auto-removes the worktree. REMOVED: /pr-merge --start mode; main-worktree guards on /test-run and /test-scenario; /test-run dev-commit + dev→staging promotion (moved to /pr-merge). v4.0.0 BREAKING: /ux-publish removed; HTML mockup generation integrated into /service-planner Step 6.
